content: The metabolism of hydrocodone involves O-demethylation, which produces hydromorphone. Hydromorphone may contribute to the overall analgesic effect of hydrocodone. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered, or close monitoring is required. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of hydromorphone by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. This interaction necessitates the use of alternative drugs or close monitoring. Cimetidine increases the effects of hydromorphone by reducing its metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of ibuprofen by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of intravenous ibuprofen by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of iloperidone by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of iloperidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of imatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of imipramine by inhibiting CYP1A2, CYP2D6, and CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. However, it decreases the levels or effects of indinavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cimetidine decreases the levels or effects of infigratinib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration with an acid-reducing agent cannot be avoided, administer infigratinib 2 hours before or 10 hours after the H2-antagonist. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of irinotecan and irinotecan liposomal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cimetidine decreases the levels or effects of iron dextran complex and iron sucrose by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Isavuconazonium sulfate may also increase the levels or effects of cimetidine through other mechanisms. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Isavuconazonium sulfate, as an OCT2 inhibitor, may increase the effects or levels of OCT2 substrates. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of cimetidine by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of isradipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of cimetidine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Istradefylline at 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of P-gp substrates in clinical trials. Dose reduction of sensitive P-gp substrates should be considered. Cimetidine decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Administer acid-neutralizing medicines at least 2 hours before or after itraconazole. When taking cimetidine, administer itraconazole with non-diet cola to increase gastrointestinal acidity. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of ivabradine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of ivabradine with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Cimetidine increases the levels of ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Reduce the ivacaftor dose if coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ivacaftor and its M1 metabolite may inhibit P-gp, potentially increasing systemic exposure to sensitive P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. However, it decreases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cimetidine decreases the levels or effects of lapatinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Lasmiditan increases the levels of cimetidine through other mechanisms. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lasmiditan inhibits BCRP in vitro. Avoid coadministration of lasmiditan with BCRP substrates. Cimetidine decreases the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir through other mechanisms. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Ledipasvir solubility decreases as pH increases; drugs that increase gastric pH are expected to decrease ledipasvir levels. H2-receptor antagonists may be administered simultaneously or 12 hours apart from ledipasvir/sofosbuvir at doses comparable to famotidine 40 mg BID. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. A lower nightly dose of lemborexant is recommended if coadministered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage modifications. Lenolisib increases the levels of cimetidine through other mechanisms. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lenolisib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase systemic exposure to BCRP substrates. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of levoketoconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. However, it decreases the levels or effects of levoketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cimetidine increases the effects of levorphanol by reducing its metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of lidocaine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Cimetidine increases the levels of lomitapide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. Lomitapide increases the levels of cimetidine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Consider reducing the dose when used concomitantly with lomitapide. Cimetidine increases the levels of lomustine by reducing its metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Enhanced myelotoxicity may occur. Cimetidine increases the levels of lonafarnib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration of lonafarnib (a sensitive CYP3A substrate) with weak CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce or continue lonafarnib at the starting dose. Closely monitor for arrhythmias and events (e.g., syncope, heart palpitations) since the effect of lonafarnib on the QT interval is unknown. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of loratadine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor. Cimetidine also increases the levels or effects of loratadine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of losartan by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. This interaction is minor. It may inhibit the conversion of losartan to its active metabolite E-3174. The importance of this interaction is not established; monitor individual therapeutic response to determine losartan dosage. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of lovastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cimetidine increases the levels of lurasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. The manufacturer recommends decreasing the starting dose of lurasidone to 20 mg/day and a maximum daily dose of 80 mg when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Concurrent use may increase the risk of lurasidone-related adverse reactions. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Initiation of weak CYP2C19 inhibitors may require a decreased mavacamten dose. Mavorixafor increases the levels of cimetidine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Caution is required if mavorixafor (a P-gp inhibitor) is coadministered with a sensitive P-gp substrate where minimal substrate concentration changes may lead to serious adverse effects. Cimetidine increases the levels of mebendazole by reducing its metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of melatonin by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Monitor melatonin effects if coadministered with moderate CYP1A2 inhibitors. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of memantine by competing for renal tubular clearance as a basic (cationic) drug. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Cimetidine increases the effects of meperidine by reducing its metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of mestranol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of metformin by competing for renal tubular clearance as a basic (cationic) drug. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of methadone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. It also increases the effects of methadone by reducing its metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of methamphetamine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Cimetidine decreases the effects of methylphenidate by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Since the characteristics of methylphenidate extended-release capsules (Ritalin LA) are pH-dependent, coadministration of antacids or acid suppressants could alter the release of methylphenidate. Consider separating the administration of the antacid and the methylphenidate extended-release capsules. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of metoprolol by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of mexiletine by inhibiting CYP1A2 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of midazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of intranasal midazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Coadministration of mild CYP3A4 inhibitors with intranasal midazolam may cause higher systemic exposure to midazolam, potentially prolonging sedation. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of midodrine by competing for renal tubular clearance as a basic (cationic) drug. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Cimetidine increases the levels of mizolastine by reducing its metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Modafinil increases the levels or effects of cimetidine by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Momelotinib increases the toxicity of cimetidine by competing for plasma protein binding. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Momelotinib, as a BCRP inhibitor, may increase the exposure of BCRP substrates.
